the_defect.why_0.0_is_not_neutral: the range of log P(Yes) is (-inf, 0], so 0.0 is the MAXIMUM of the range: P(Yes)=1.0, maximally alarming. measured_on_one_dry_cell.what: the episode-boundary question behind open ruling 2: how often the 40-entry stream window spans more than one EP-G episode, with the device score channel live
measured_on_one_dry_cell.cell: seed 4, 4 devices, 300 s, 40:40:20, lh_req, ss2, epg, per-frame, reask 30.0, dry
measured_on_one_dry_cell.why_it_matters: both cards specify a WITHIN-CLIP trajectory (inarvl A1 substitutes for ONE image; hybrid_llm A4 is offsets of ONE clip), and the harness window does not respect clip or episode boundaries

before_side_of_the_decision_diff_cannot_.consequence: both sides of the item (c) diff must be run at ONE sha, from two trees differing only in the D201 patch. This is CLAUDE.md consistency check 7: a side of the comparison that is never audited.

open_rulings: D201 names two arms; seven read the values, and baselines/constructed.py:110 (B4) is ours, not a published baseline. Whether the other five arms' committed cells are superseded, and whether B4's are, is a user decision.

Both cards specify a within-clip trajectory and the harness window crosses episode boundaries in 96.2 per cent of calls (see measured_on_one_dry_cell). Whether to slice the two arms' feature window to the current episode changes both arms' decisions and is not decided here.

A synthetic trace holds no committed device score, so once scores are real no arm whose published method reads one can run on a synthetic cell; tests/test_live2_coord.py's all-arm legality and fairness tests run every registered arm on exactly such a trace.
